vendor: Block (now under the Agentic AI Foundation / Linux Foundation, repo org `aaif-goose`)
repo: https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose (upstream was github.com/block/goose, redirects to aaif-goose/goose). Workspace version 1.55.0 per root Cargo.toml `workspace.package.version`; Cargo.lock pins sqlx 0.9.0, rmcp 3.4.1, etcetera 0.11.0.
surfaces: CLI (Rust, `goose`), Desktop (Tauri, same storage dir), ACP server, goose-server. CLI and Desktop share one sessions.db.
binaries: `goose.exe` (CLI), `goose` on Unix/macOS; Desktop ships a separate GUI binary. Upstream package names: `goose-cli` crate, `goose` crate.

paths: %APPDATA%\Block\goose\data\sessions\<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>.jsonl  (LEGACY pre-1.10.0 per-session files; left on disk, no longer written/maintained)
%APPDATA%\Block\goose\data\logs\  (text logs; `llm_request.*.jsonl` holds RAW LLM prompts - MUST NOT be used)
%USERPROFILE%\.local\share\goose\sessions\  (NOT the Windows path - that is the Unix XDG path; goose on Windows never used it)
storage.format: SQLite 3 database, one shared file for ALL sessions, WAL journal mode. No per-project subdirectories, no per-session files. `messages.content_json` is a JSON *array* of internally-tagged content blocks (serde tag="type", rename_all="camelCase"): text | thinking | toolRequest | toolResponse | image | document | toolConfirmationRequest | actionRequired | systemNotification | error. Tool call shape: {"type":"toolRequest","id":"<call id>","toolCall":{"status":"success","value":{"name":"write","arguments":{...}}}}. Schema version is already 17 and goose ships ALTER TABLE migrations, so columns churn. Pre-v1.10.0 the format was per-session `.jsonl` (line 1 = session metadata JSON, following lines = message JSON, filename `%Y%m%d_%H%M%S`) - that legacy format IS append-only line-delimited and would fit Discodex's existing LogTailer, but goose no longer writes it.
storage.append_semantics: NOT append-only and NOT line-delimited. Every message is a single `INSERT INTO messages (...)` executed inside its own `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction, plus `UPDATE sessions SET updated_at = datetime('now')` (SessionStorage::add_message). The file is therefore mutated live during a run, but as binary SQLite pages committed into `sessions.db-wal`, not as newline-terminated records. The existing LogTailer (byte-offset cursor + split on '\n') cannot read it; a binary SQLite file also has no line boundaries at all.
storage.session_file_naming: No per-session file. Session id is `YYYYMMDD_N` (e.g. `20251021_1`, created as `<YYYYMMDD>_<counter>` in create_session). sessions.session_type in (user, scheduled, subagent, hidden, terminal, gateway, acp). Subagents are child sessions linked by sessions.parent_session_id. sessions.project_id is an optional named goose "project" (goose `sources`); otherwise sessions are grouped by sessions.working_dir. messages.id is a global AUTOINCREMENT integer and is the only reliable monotonic event cursor.

fields.project: YES. sessions.working_dir holds the absolute workspace path (e.g. C:\Users\PC\Documents\Discodex). Only the final folder name may be published (Discodex's SessionMetadata.project). sessions.project_id is an optional user-defined goose project id.
fields.model: YES. sessions.provider_name (e.g. "openai", "anthropic", "openrouter") + sessions.model_config_json -> {"model_name":"gpt-5-codex", ...}. usage_ledger.model holds the model per request. Discodex publishes model ids through ParsedEvent::AgentDetected{agent}, same as Codex/Claude Code.
fields.file_basename: YES. The developer platform extension is FLAT (tool names: write, edit, shell, tree, read_image) and file tools use the argument key "path" (FileWriteParams{path,content}, FileEditParams{path,before,after}). Discodex's existing extract_file_basename() already probes "path", so it works unchanged - but only the basename may be forwarded.
fields.tool_activity: YES. messages.content_json toolRequest blocks carry toolCall.value.name and toolCall.value.arguments; toolResponse blocks (stored in a message whose role is "user") mark tool completion and carry the call id. MCP extension tools are namespaced as <extension>__<tool> (e.g. registered__tool).
fields.phase: YES. A message with role="user" containing a text block = a human prompt (new turn -> TaskStarted). A toolRequest = tool running (RunningTools). An assistant message whose blocks are only text (no pending tool requests) = turn finished (Completed). Goose also has a final_output / recipe__final_output tool.
fields.timestamps: YES. messages.created_timestamp is an INTEGER epoch-seconds value (Message.created; goose clamps it to be non-decreasing within a session). messages.timestamp is SQLite CURRENT_TIMESTAMP text (UTC). sessions.created_at / updated_at are SQLite CURRENT_TIMESTAMP text. Reading back uses ORDER BY created_timestamp, id. messages.id (AUTOINCREMENT) is the global insertion-order cursor and is the right poll key.

parser_strategy:
RECOMMENDED: a dedicated SQLite reader that bypasses the line-based pipeline entirely, reusing Discodex's existing helpers (classify_tool, extract_file_basename, language_from_file) and the existing ParsedEvent/ActivityState machinery.

1) New module src/goose_db.rs owning a `GooseReader` with: db path, `last_message_id: i64` cursor, and a `poll(now_ms) -> Vec<ParsedEvent>` method.
2) Open read-only: `rusqlite::Connection::open_with_flags(path, SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY | SQLITE_OPEN_URI)` + `PRAGMA query_only=true` + `PRAGMA busy_timeout=2000`. WAL readers never block the goose writer. If the read-only open fails (missing/stale -shm, permissions), fall back to copying sessions.db + sessions.db-wal (+ -shm) into %TEMP%\discodex-goose-snap\ and reading the copy (never write to goose's dir; never take a write lock on its DB).
3) Query: SELECT m.id, m.session_id, m.role, m.content_json, m.created_timestamp, s.working_dir, s.provider_name, s.model_config_json, s.session_type, s.parent_session_id FROM messages m JOIN sessions s ON s.id = m.session_id WHERE m.id > ? ORDER BY m.id LIMIT 500. Cursor = last m.id.
4) Per row, decode content_json into blocks and emit ParsedEvents:
   - once per session: SessionMetadata{project: basename(working_dir), cwd: working_dir}
   - session row provider_name/model_config_json.model_name -> AgentDetected{agent: "<model id>"} (Discodex already uses AgentDetected to surface models)
   - role="user" row whose blocks include a text block -> TaskStarted{started_at_ms: created_timestamp*1000}
   - block type "thinking" -> Thinking{reasoning: None}  (do NOT ship reasoning prose; optional: reuse events::extract_reasoning_summary on a sanitized/truncated string, same policy as other providers)
   - block type "toolRequest" -> TrackedToolStarted{call_id: block.id, activity: ToolActivity{label: classify_tool(name, ""), file: extract_file_basename(arguments), language: language_from_file(file)}}. Tool names are flat (write/edit/shell/tree/read_image) so classify_tool already maps write|edit -> "Editing files", read_image -> "Inspecting image"; add a goose-specific branch for "tree" -> "Exploring project" and map "shell" WITHOUT passing the raw command.
   - block type "toolResponse" -> TrackedToolFinished{call_id: block.id}
   - assistant row with only text blocks -> Completed
   - sessions.session_type="subagent" -> SubagentSpawned{conversation_id: parent_session_id, agent: "goose subagent"}
5) Trigger: on the existing notify watcher, intercept any path under the goose session root that is sessions.db / -wal / -shm and re-run poll() instead of tailer.read_new(). Add a 1-2 s poll as a safety net (SQLite WAL writes do not always surface as a distinct notify event).
6) Do NOT reuse the legacy .jsonl path for live activity: pre-1.10.0 files are static. They can optionally be parsed at startup for history only, using the same line-based contract (line 1 = metadata, later lines = messages) - but that is a separate, optional code path.

LEGACY JSONL (optional, history only): parse_line_for(Provider::Goose) could read a .jsonl line: first line = session metadata -> SessionMetadata; later lines = a serialized Message -> same block mapping. This would be the only way to keep the existing parse_line_for shape, but it yields no live activity on goose >= 1.10.0.

CHANGES TO watcher.rs / main.rs (REQUIRED - this is the whole point)
The existing LogTailer is byte-offset + split('\n') and cannot read a binary SQLite file. Required work:
1. New dependency: `rusqlite = { version = "0.37", features = ["bundled"] }` (bundled compiles SQLite from C source; needs the MSVC toolchain the user already has; adds ~1-3 min build time and ~1.5 MB to the binary). Alternatives are worse: `sqlx` is async and heavy, the `sqlite` crate needs a system SQLite that stock Windows lacks, and shelling out to sqlite3.exe is not viable. FLAG THIS COST explicitly.
2. New file src/goose_db.rs: GooseReader { db_path, last_message_id } with poll(now_ms) -> Vec<ParsedEvent> (read-only open, WAL-safe, cursor on messages.id).
3. watcher.rs: LogTailer/recent_logs/collect_logs are JSONL-only. Do not route sessions.db through them. Either (a) keep session_sources() for the four existing harnesses and register the goose source separately as a "db source", or (b) generalize SessionSource with a `kind: LogKind::{Tail, Sqlite}` field. Option (a) is less invasive.
4. main.rs worker loop: in the WorkerEvent::Paths branch, if the changed path is the goose sessions.db/-wal/-shm, call goose_reader.poll() and apply the resulting ParsedEvents instead of tailer.read_new(). Add a periodic poll (1-2 s) as a safety net, because WAL writes do not always produce a distinct notify event. The existing notify watch on the session root already covers the goose directory, so no new watcher is needed - only a different reaction to the same events.
5. main.rs startup scan: for goose, do NOT use recent_logs(); instead open the DB once, read the last N sessions/messages (ORDER BY m.id DESC LIMIT n) to seed project/model, and let poll() take over.

FORMAT-CHURN RISK AND FAIL-SAFE
- goose is on schema version 17 and adds columns via ALTER TABLE migrations every few releases. Our SELECT names columns explicitly, so ADDED columns are harmless, but a RENAMED/REMOVED column breaks the query.
  Fail-safe: run the query in two tiers - (1) full column set; (2) on error, retry with the minimal set (m.id, m.session_id, m.role, m.content_json, m.created_timestamp) and fetch session columns with a separate tolerant query, defaulting missing values. If the tables/columns are missing entirely, log once, mark the goose source unavailable, and disable it - never crash the tray app and never publish a guessed value.
- content_json block types can change (upstream already migrated "reasoning" -> "thinking"). Fail-safe: unknown block types are IGNORED, never forwarded, and never cause an error.
- The DB path could change (the "Block" segment is explicitly kept "for backwards compatibility" in paths.rs). Fail-safe: probe a small list of candidate roots each startup; if none has sessions.db, disable the goose source silently.
- Never write to goose's DB, never take a write lock, never DELETE rows. Open read-only; if that fails, read a temp copy.
- If a goose session's working_dir no longer exists, do not publish it.
- Unknown session_type values -> treat as "user" rather than erroring.

risks: FORMAT MISMATCH (the real blocker): the adapter contract is built around append-only, newline-delimited text (LogTailer byte cursor + split('\n')). Goose's live store is a binary SQLite database. The existing tailer cannot read it at all - not 'awkwardly', literally: there are no line boundaries in a SQLite file. A Goose adapter needs a NEW reader class and a NEW dependency, not just a new Provider variant.

NEW DEPENDENCY: rusqlite (bundled SQLite) must be added to Cargo.toml. Cost: a C build of SQLite (~1-3 min extra build time, needs the MSVC toolchain), ~1.5 MB binary growth, plus a read-only WAL-safe connection strategy. There is no way to read this DB with the current dependency set.

PATH CORRECTION: the assigned path %USERPROFILE%\.local\share\goose is the Unix XDG path and is WRONG for Windows. Windows goose uses %APPDATA%\Block\goose\data\sessions\sessions.db (i.e. C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\Block\goose\data\sessions\sessions.db). Using the assigned path would find nothing on a Windows box.

SQLITE vs JSONL: the assigned 'sqlite vs jsonl' question resolves to 'sqlite since v1.10.0' (current upstream 1.55.0). The .jsonl format is legacy-only, frozen, and not written any more - a JSONL adapter would show no live activity.

PRIVACY: the DB contains the full conversation. content_json holds user prompts, assistant answers, model reasoning, raw tool arguments and raw tool output (including file contents). Only structural facts may be extracted. Specifically forbidden: text blocks, thinking text, toolResult contents, shell command strings, the sessions.name field (goose auto-generates it from the prompt), and the directory part of any path.

TOOL NAME SEMANTICS: goose's developer extension is FLAT (write/edit/shell/tree/read_image), so the tool name alone does not tell you which file - the file comes from arguments.path. MCP extension tools are namespaced <extension>__<tool>, so a bare name match can collide with an extension tool of the same name.

ROLE SEMANTICS: goose stores tool observations under role="user". A naive 'role=user means the human typed something' rule would fire a spurious TaskStarted on every tool result. The parser must look at the block types, not the role alone.

POLL LATENCY: unlike a JSONL tailer that reacts to a notify event instantly, a SQLite reader must be polled (or woken by a -wal file event). Budget 1-2 s of latency, or accept a busier watcher. WAL writes also do not always produce a distinct notify event, so a timer is required as a safety net.

SCHEMA CHURN: goose is at schema version 17 and ships ALTER TABLE migrations regularly. Column renames will break a strict SELECT; the parser must degrade gracefully and disable the source rather than crash or publish garbage.
LEGACY PATH DEAD END: supporting only the .jsonl legacy files would be 'partial' at best and would show nothing for any goose >= 1.10.0 user. Do not ship a JSONL-only Goose adapter.
NAME COLLISION: 'goose' is a common word; a loose window-title match would fire on unrelated apps and browser tabs (e.g. 'Canada Goose'). Use whole-word matching and add negative tests.
confidence: High for storage location, format, schema and live-write semantics (all read from upstream source at main + official docs, cross-checked). Medium-high for the exact serialized JSON shape of content_json (derived from upstream serde attributes and rmcp's CallToolRequestParams, not from a captured row). Medium for the Discodex-side integration specifics (read from the local repo, but no prototype was built and no goose install was inspected, per the instruction to research upstream only).
summary: Block Goose is NOT cloud-only - it stores every session locally, so it qualifies on criterion 1. But the local store is a single SQLite database (WAL mode), NOT JSONL: since goose v1.10.0 all sessions live in one `sessions.db`; the old per-session `.jsonl` files are legacy and are no longer written. On Windows the path is %APPDATA%\Block\goose\data\sessions\sessions.db - NOT %USERPROFILE%\.local\share\goose (that is the Unix XDG path; goose on Windows never used it). The DB is written LIVE (one INSERT per message, in its own transaction, during the run) and carries everything Discodex needs: sessions.working_dir (project), sessions.provider_name + model_config_json.model_name (model), messages.content_json toolRequest blocks with flat tool names (write/edit/shell/tree/read_image) and a "path" argument (current file basename), toolResponse blocks (tool finished), and role/timestamps for phase + timer. The catch is architectural: the existing LogTailer/parse_line_for contract is line-delimited text, so Goose needs a SQLite reader (new dependency rusqlite, read-only + WAL-safe, cursor on messages.id) and a separate polling path in watcher.rs/main.rs. All metadata is recoverable WITHOUT shipping conversation text, so the privacy rules are satisfiable. Verdict: rich - but the integration is a new adapter class, not a new Provider variant alone.
